refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: vera logs all runlevel switches, this includes system startup and shutdown. The logs are retained for a set number of days, the oldest log files get automatically removed at system startup. The number of days of log retention is controlled by the SWITCHLOGDAYS environment variable. vlad setenv SWITCHLOGDAYS 5 sets the retention period to five days. At most five days of logs are kept (dates without logs don't count toward the limit).

note.para: There will be an extra day of logs at times. Logs get purged at system boot before a new log gets created, possibly for a brand new day.

refsect1.para: The logs command lists all available switch logs, from the oldest to the newest. It produces the following output:

listitem.para: The log number. The logs are numbered from the newest to the oldest, so log #1 is always the most recent log.
The timestamp of each runlevel switch.

refsect1.para: The log files record low-level details and times, the vlad log command reads log file #1, the most recent log file, and processes the logs into a basic list of units and how long it took for each unit to start. An optional parameter reads a different log file. vlad log 2 reads log file #2.
The log command produces a listing of units that were started or stopped, one unit per line. Each line contains:

listitem.para: How long the unit's starting or stopping command took to run to completion.
How long the unit waited for other units to start or stop, before it could start or stop.

refsect1.para: An asterisk, * appears at the beginning of the line of the unit that took the longest time to start or stop. The asterisk's only purpose is to identify the unit with the longest starting or stopping time.

refsect1.title: BUGS
refsect1.para: system/inittab/rc is often listed as the slowest-starting unit. The actual culprit will be some other unit that gets started by system/inittab/rc. This is an artifact of how the inittab command converts the init scripts to vera units.
